title: Concrete Lining Thickness — Minimum (USBR)

D_n.description: Normal depth of flow in canal

applicability: USBR guideline for unreinforced concrete. Practical range: 50–150 mm. Larger canals (Q > 30 m³/s) typically 100–150 mm. Add reinforcement or increase thickness for differential settlement, frost, or uplift.
source: USBR Design Standards, Aisenbrey et al. (1978)

title: Seepage Loss Through Lined Canal

q.description: Seepage rate per unit wetted area

applicability: For estimating total seepage. Seepage rate q depends on lining type, condition, and groundwater level. Rate increases with head differential and deterioration of lining.

title: Hydrostatic Uplift on Empty Canal Lining

FS_uplift.description: Factor of safety against lining blowout (≥ 1.3–1.5)

W_lining.description: Weight of lining per unit area

W_soil_cover.description: Weight of soil cover over membrane (if any)

α.description: Slope angle of canal side (from horizontal)

applicability: Critical when canal is drained for maintenance or during low-flow periods. Underdrain system required when FS < 1.5 without drainage.

title: Seepage Through Concrete Lining (Darcy's Law)

k_lining.description: Hydraulic conductivity of concrete lining (typically 10⁻⁸ to 10⁻⁶ cm/s)

h.description: Head of water above lining invert

applicability: Assumes saturated flow through lining. Actual seepage is dominated by joints and cracks, not concrete permeability. Total seepage = lining seepage + joint seepage.

title: Economic Lining Thickness Optimization

C_total.description: Total annualized cost per unit length

C_lining.description: Capital cost of lining (increases with thickness)

C_seepage.description: Value of water lost through seepage (decreases with thickness)

C_maintenance.description: Annual maintenance cost (decreases with thicker/better lining)

applicability: Optimal thickness minimizes total annualized cost. For irrigation: value of water = crop revenue per m³ × seepage volume. Economic analysis must include discount rate and design life.

title: Concrete Joint Spacing (Thermal Contraction)
equation: L_joint ≤ 2 × √(f_t × t / (E × α_T × ΔT × γ_c × μ))

ΔT.description: Temperature drop from placement to service

μ.description: Coefficient of friction between lining and subgrade (0.5–1.5)

applicability: Simplified approach. Practical joint spacing: 3–5 m for unreinforced concrete. USBR typically specifies 3.0–3.7 m (10–12 ft). Wider spacing requires reinforcement to control crack widths.

title: Geomembrane Anchor Trench Depth

T_pullout.description: Pullout force on membrane (from wind, thermal, or water)

applicability: Simplified. Typical anchor trench: 300–600 mm deep × 300 mm wide, backfilled with compacted soil. Membrane extends into trench, folds back, and is buried. USBR and geomembrane manufacturer guidelines provide detailed anchor trench designs.

title: Slip-Form Paving Production Rate
equation: P_daily = v_pave × P_canal × t × 8 hr × η_production

P_canal.description: Canal perimeter being paved per pass

applicability: Large canal lining projects use specialized slip-form machines that place, vibrate, and finish concrete in one pass. Typical output: 150–500 m³/day for large-canal operations.
